transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2025-09-03 15:00 PDT
- Duration: 57 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Alex Rivera (Head of AI - Greenpoint), Priya Nair (Infra Lead), Samir Patel (PM), Renee Ortiz (Security)

Summary:
Quick scoping session to align on POC success criteria (latency, cost per 1M tokens, throughput), workload sizing and dataset for bench, and decision criteria between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Security constraints (KMS, audit logs), timeline for 4-week POC, and owners for data collection and bench run were decided.

Topics discussed:
- POC goals: production-like throughput, acceptance criteria for p50/p95 latency, cost targets and regression tolerances
- Workload sizing: expected qps, average and max sequence lengths, concurrency patterns (batch vs single requests)
- Benchmarks: synthetic vs replay from traces, prefixes/kv cache re-use, evaluation metrics (latency, tokens/sec, cost estimates)
additional_transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We wanted to use this time to make sure we got a concrete outline for the POC: what success looks like, what data you can share, and any constraints around network and keys. Alex, want to kick off with current goals?

[00:18] Alex (Greenpoint): Yeah, thanks. Uh, we, uh, we're trying to decide whether to go straight to a private on-prem setup or start hosted and then maybe move to dedicated. Key constraint is that our edge sites need sub-200ms for suggested delivery for routing recommendations. Cost is also a hard factor — we have to justify per-invoice savings to ops.

[00:42] Priya (Infra): To add, we have pockets of limited network egress at two hubs, so we can't assume high throughput to the cloud in all regions. We also have strict key management requirements — our KMS is vendor X and must be used for any persistent storage.

[01:05] Diego (Redwood SE): Okay, that helps. For the POC we usually run three profiles: hosted baseline, dedicated reserved sizing, and a private-onprem sim with our private control plane. For each we measure p50/p95 latency, cost-per-token estimate, throughput at target concurrency, and failure/fallback behavior.

[01:30] Samir (PM): What does the private sim mean? Are you actually installing anything in our DC for a 4-week POC?

[01:36] Diego: For the POC we can do either a lightweight VM bundle that mimics private networking and KMS integration, or if you prefer, we can run a dockerized on-prem trial. But often customers start with hosted to get quick signals then move to dedicated or private once they confirm economics.

[01:55] Renee (Security): We need logs at token level? Audit trail is critical. Also what about SOC2 and ISO attestation from Redwood? We can't move forward without that.

[02:06] Maya: Yes, we'll share the SOC2 report and our network diagram. We also support KMS integrations; for the POC we can wire up a test key with your KMS to validate encryption at rest.

[02:20] Alex: Great. For success criteria: p95 under 220ms for inference at target concurrency, throughput >= 600 qps aggregate for our pilot subset, and cost less than $X per 1M tokens — we need ballpark numbers to present to finance. Also no quality regressions beyond 2% on our eval prompts.

[02:45] Diego: Noted. Couple clarifying questions: when you say 600 qps, is that steady-state or spike? And average token length?

[02:53] Priya: That's peak during daytime windows, steady-state is ~200 qps. Avg seq length is roughly 80 tokens, tail up to 400 for some long bills. Most requests are single-turn, a small % are multi-turn.

[03:15] Diego: Perfect. For benchmarking we'll need 7 days of traces — p95 arrival rate, sequence length histogram, and payload examples. We'll do both replay and synthetic (to stress peak), and include prefix/K-V cache reuse scenarios since you mentioned multi-turn.

[03:36] Samir: How do you treat KV cache in hosted vs dedicated vs private? I mean, will caching behavior change latency and cost materially?

[03:44] Diego: Yes. Hosted includes our automated prefix caching and transparent KV reuse; dedicated gives you persistent KV caching in the reserved pool which often reduces p95 under heavy concurrency. Private can be configured the same way but depends on your infra — e.g., affinity, local NVMe caches. So we'll profile both cold and warm cache scenarios.

[04:05] Alex: OK. About the benchmarks, what's the template you need?

[04:10] Maya: We'll send a short data template. It asks for token histograms, request timestamps, sample payloads, and any special preprocessing steps. We usually also ask for the top 50 eval prompts you care about for quality regression checks.

[04:25] Renee: On compliance, we need to see audit logging granularity — who can access prompt data, retention windows, and redaction options. Can Redwood redact PII on ingestion?

[04:36] Maya: We have configurable retention and redaction hooks; for PII we can apply redaction in the ingestion pipeline or at the customer side before sending. We'll include documentation and examples.

[04:50] Priya: Another question — for Dedicated, what are the autoscaling options? We don't want unpredictable bursting costs.

[04:57] Diego: Dedicated supports scheduled scaling and burst capacity within agreed limits. For the POC we can simulate your baseline and a burst scenario. Billing for Dedicated is a committed monthly capacity plus a small overage model in the pilot. We'll provide a cost model in the benchmark report.

[05:19] Alex: On timelines, we're targeting an internal decision by 10/03. Can the POC run in 3 weeks or do you need 4?

[05:27] Diego: Realistically, 4 weeks gives us time for data collection, bench runs, and a regression eval. But if you can deliver traces fast (by 9/07) and unblock KMS test keys we can accelerate to ~3 weeks.

[05:39] Samir: Are there typical failure modes we should watch for when we move from hosted to private? Network latency, KV syncing?

[05:47] Diego: Yeah, network latency and serialization of cache snapshots can cause tail latency. Also model variant mismatches — if you use quantized variants on private hardware, output could differ slightly. We'll include quality drift checks in the bench.

[06:05] Renee: One more: do you need us to open firewall rules? We have strict egress controls.

[06:11] Maya: We'll provide an allowlist of endpoints. For hosted flows you'll need outbound to Redwood API endpoints; for private we coordinate with your infra to avoid unwanted egress.

[06:22] Alex: I'd like to hear a concrete success rubric — can we codify it now?

[06:26] Maya: Sure, proposed POC acceptance criteria: 1) p95 latency <= 220ms for the warm cache profile at 600 qps peak, 2) system handles steady-state 200 qps for 24 hours with <1% error rate, 3) cost per 1M tokens projection below your threshold — we'll put numbers after initial bench, 4) no quality regression >2% on your eval set. If those are met we recommend proceeding to Dedicated or Private based on economics and compliance.

[06:52] Priya: That looks reasonable. For the private option, we need an on-site checklist: KMS integration steps, network ACLs, hardware requirements (GPUs), and quantization support.

[07:03] Diego: We'll include a private deployment checklist. For hardware we typically recommend N GPUs of X type based on your concurrency and model choice; we'll surface those after initial bench.

[07:15] Alex: Competitors question — we've had evals with Anthropic and a couple of cloud vendors. How do you compare on latency/cost?

[07:23] Maya: High level: our hosting is tuned for lower tail latency via continuous batching and KV caching; dedicated gives you better unit economics for sustained workloads. We'll include a competitor slide but won't do a full bake-off without your permission.

[07:38] Samir: Regarding data retention: if we choose Hosted initially, can we opt for a VPC peering later?

[07:44] Maya: Yes, Hosted to Dedicated to Private is a supported growth path; you can pin model versions and move traffic with rollout policies. We'll show the migration path in the POC report.

[07:58] Priya: For the bench itself, how do you estimate cost? Is it based on tokens or GPU hours?

[08:03] Diego: For hosted we show tokens-based cost projection. For dedicated/private we give a combined model: amortized infra cost (GPU hours) plus operational overhead; we translate that back to a per-1M-token equivalent so finance can compare apples-to-apples.

[08:20] Renee: Please include encryption-at-rest diagrams and KMS call flows. That's blocker for Legal.

[08:26] Maya: Understood. We'll send the security packet and a draft runbook.

[08:32] Alex: Ok, last quick thing — what are the typical knobs you tune to hit p95? Is it batching, quantization, or routing?

[08:39] Diego: All of those. For p95 we tune batch sizes, model variants (FP16 vs int8), KV cache warmup policies, and request routing to lower-latency pools. We'll run ablations in the bench to show tradeoffs.

[08:55] Maya: Great. To recap and owners — Maya will send benchmark plan and security docs by EOD 9/04, Diego will prepare the latency/throughput target sheet, Priya will provide traces by 9/07, Renee will confirm KMS constraints by 9/04, and we schedule the bench kickoff for week of 9/08.

[09:15] Alex: Sounds good. Anything else?

[09:19] Samir: No, that's it from product.

[09:23] Renee: Thanks — looking forward to the security materials.

[09:26] Maya: Thank you everyone. We'll follow up with invites and the data template.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription: occasional crosstalk, small mis-hearings ("K-V cash" for KV cache), and filler words retained where relevant. The technical team emphasized p95 targets and sample traces are the critical inputs to avoid benching on unrealistic synthetic loads.

References/Links mentioned:

Decisions made during call:

- Success criteria drafted and owners assigned.
